newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Friday, as traders expected the market to continue to trade sideways in its recent 155.00-165.00 cents per lb range basis September.

New York arabica prices ended weaker in dull, local-dominated trading on Thursday. September fell 1.05 cents a lb, to 160.45 cents, after ranging between 163.50 and 159.00 cents. Spot July, which expires on Monday, ended 0.35 cents weaker, at 186.90 cents, while the outer months closed down 0.25 to 1.45 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 26.45 cents compared with 25.75 cents at the close on Wednesday, while the September/December switch narrowed to 12.85 cents from 13.20 cents.
CSCE reported after Thursday's close that certified coffee inventories rose by 1,737 60-kg bags as of July 16, to 77,151 bags. An additional 36,587 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday that there is no cold weather expected through the middle of next week in Brazil's coffee belt, with temperatures in major coffee-growing areas likely to range in the low 50s to the low 60s F (12-16 C) through Wednesday.
Technically, traders said September still faced support at 155.00 cents, with the next level seen at 150.00 cents. Resistance was seen near 165.00 cents.
London robusta futures were broadly lower early Friday in light trading. At the midday break, benchmark September was down $25 at $1,570, after ranging from $1,590 to $1,570.
